Panel graphical VAR network (panel-GVAR)

Source: R/panelgvar.R
panel_gvar.Rd

Estimates the three networks of the panel graphical vector-autoregressive model (Epskamp 2020) from few-wave, many-person panel data: a directed temporal network (within-person lag-1 effects), an undirected contemporaneous network (partial correlations of the within-person innovations), and an undirected between-person network (partial correlations of the stable person means). The within-person process is a stationary VAR(1) around a random intercept; means are stationary across waves. This is the model fitted by psychonetrics::panelgvar(), estimated by maximum likelihood in base R.

Usage

panel_gvar(
  data,
  vars,
  id = NULL,
  wave = NULL,
  select = c("none", "prune", "ebic"),
  alpha = 0.01,
  adjust = "none",
  recursive = FALSE,
  stepup = TRUE,
  criterion = c("bic", "none"),
  gamma = 0.5,
  nlambda = 50L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 1e-04,
  refit = FALSE,
  standardize = c("none", "z", "z_per_wave"),
  labels = NULL,
  na_method = "listwise"
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame (or matrix). Either long (one row per person per wave; give vars, id, wave) or wide (one row per person; give vars as a design matrix).

vars

Long data: character vector of the variable columns. Wide data: a character matrix of column names, one row per variable and one column per wave (the psychonetrics vars design); its row names become the labels.

id, wave

Long data only: names of the person-identifier and wave columns. Person identifiers must be non-missing. Waves are ordered by sort() (or factor level order).

select

Edge selection. "none" (default): every edge is estimated and reported with its standard error and p-value – significance is shown, not imposed (the psychonetrics default). "prune": remove edges with p > alpha and refit, then step up (see stepup) – psychonetrics' prune() |> stepup(). "ebic": penalized maximum likelihood (lasso on every temporal, contemporaneous and between parameter) with the penalty chosen by EBIC along a path – psychonetrics' panelgvar(estimator = "PML"), the panel counterpart of ebic_glasso().

alpha

Significance level for the significant flag, the solid/dashed edges of plot(), and select = "prune". Default 0.01 (psychonetrics::prune()'s default).

adjust

Multiplicity correction applied to the edge p-values before pruning, one of stats::p.adjust.methods. Default "none" (psychonetrics::prune()'s default).

recursive

Logical; repeat pruning until no edge has p > alpha. Default FALSE.

stepup

Logical; after pruning, run the psychonetrics::stepup() search: re-add the pruned edge with the largest modification index while it is significant at alpha and the refit passes a chi-square difference test at alpha (and lowers BIC, with criterion = "bic"). Default TRUE, because one-pass pruning can remove parameters that substitute for each other (e.g. an autoregression and correlated cross-lagged effects), each non-significant alone but not jointly. FALSE reproduces psychonetrics::prune() alone. Used only with select = "prune".

criterion

Step-up acceptance criterion besides the chi-square test: "bic" (default, as psychonetrics::stepup()) or "none".

gamma, nlambda, lambda_min_ratio

For select = "ebic": the EBIC hyperparameter (default 0.5), the number of penalty values on the path (50; a finite integer >= 2) and the smallest as a fraction of the largest (1e-4) – psychonetrics' find_penalized_lambda() defaults.

refit

For select = "ebic": refit the selected network by unpenalized maximum likelihood (standard errors and p-values then come from that refit). Default FALSE: the penalized estimates are returned, and standard errors, p-values and significant are NA (they do not apply to lasso estimates).

standardize

Rescale the data before fitting, as psychonetrics' panelvar(standardize =): "none" (default), "z" (one mean and SD per variable, pooled over waves), or "z_per_wave" (z-score every variable separately within every wave). "z_per_wave" removes wave-to-wave drift in means and variances – useful when the stationary-means assumption fails, at the price of no longer modelling that drift – and makes the edges standardized. Standardization uses the available values (SD with denominator n - 1) before listwise deletion.

labels

Optional node labels (default: vars for long data, the design row names for wide data).

na_method

Missing-data handling. Only "listwise" is supported: a person missing any wave/variable is dropped (with a warning giving the count). A pairwise covariance is not a likelihood for this model and full- information ML is not yet implemented, so "pairwise" is refused.

Value

An object of class c("psychnet_panelgvar", "netobject_group"): a named list of three psychnet networks, temporal (directed; edge from -> to weight beta[to, from], autoregressive effects kept in $beta), contemporaneous, and between (undirected partial correlations; the innovation / between covariance in $sigma). Being a netobject_group, it plots as a grid with cograph::splot(). Read it with as.data.frame(): what = "edges" (one row per edge with standard error, p-value and 95% Wald interval), what = "parameters" (every model parameter), what = "fit" (one row of fit indices: chi-square, CFI, TLI, RMSEA, AIC, BIC), what = "variance" (one row per variable: the between-person share of its variance), or what = "diagnostics" (one row: the score certificate – largest absolute gradient of the ML fit function on the free parameters, or the lasso KKT residual for select = "ebic" – boundary flag, SE availability, and how many of the three optimizer starts reached the best optimum). Fitting, inference and the certificate run on standardized variables (pooled SD per variable), so they are unit-free and the certificate does not depend on the variables' units; the model is scale-equivariant, so estimates and standard errors map back exactly and are returned on the data scale.

Errors are classed: psychnet_bad_input for unusable input (fewer than three waves, too few persons, non-numeric or missing columns, a requested "pairwise"), psychnet_no_converge if the optimizer ends at an infeasible point. Warnings are classed too: psychnet_no_converge (score above 1e-6 at an interior solution), psychnet_boundary (the final contemporaneous or between covariance is near-singular, i.e. partial correlations near +/-1 – common with three waves; those estimates are unreliable, and the score, which need not vanish there, is quoted in the message), psychnet_singular_information (some parameters are not identified at the returned estimate: their standard errors are NA, the others exact), psychnet_approximate_se (the fit being pruned had a singular information; the parameters it does not identify were treated as having infinite standard errors, so pruning removes them), and psychnet_listwise_drop (persons removed for missing values).

Details

By default the full (saturated) model is returned: every edge with its standard error, p-value, 95% Wald interval and a significant flag at alpha, drawn solid (significant) or dashed (not) by plot().

select = "ebic" instead minimizes F + lambda * sum|theta| over the temporal (autoregressive diagonal included), contemporaneous and between parameters, for 50 log-spaced lambdas from the smallest penalty that empties every network, keeping the lambda with the lowest EBIC = -2 logL + k log n

  • 4 k gamma log V (k free parameters, V wave x variable columns). The solver (accelerated proximal gradient, then an active-set Newton polish) stays inside the model's domain and is certified by the lasso KKT conditions; the selected lambda is re-solved from three starts. The likelihood is not convex, so the certificate proves a stationary point, and print() reports how many starts agree.

With select = "prune" the saturated model is fitted, every temporal, contemporaneous, and between edge whose Wald p-value exceeds alpha is fixed to zero in a single pass, and the model is refitted – the psychonetrics::prune() default workflow (recursive = TRUE repeats until every remaining edge is significant). Then, with stepup = TRUE (default), the psychonetrics::stepup() search adds pruned edges back one at a time while modification indices, chi-square difference tests and BIC support them, so select = "prune" equals psychonetrics' panelgvar() |> runmodel() |> prune() |> stepup().

References

Epskamp, S. (2020). Psychometric network models from time-series and panel data. Psychometrika, 85(1), 206-231. doi:10.1007/s11336-020-09697-3

Examples

# srl_panel: 100 students x 4 weeks, simulated from a panel-GVAR in which
# effort in one week drives efficacy in the next.
fit <- panel_gvar(srl_panel,
                  vars = c("efficacy", "planning", "effort", "enjoyment",
                           "anxiety"),
                  id = "student", wave = "week")
fit
#> <psychnet_panelgvar> panel graphical VAR (temporal + contemporaneous + between)
#>   persons: 100   waves: 4   nodes: 5
#>   edges (significant/estimated, p < 0.01): temporal 1/20 (+4/5 autoregressive)   contemporaneous 5/10   between 2/10
#>   selection: none (full model)
#>   fit: chisq(170) = 207.19, p = 0.0273   CFI = 0.957   TLI = 0.946   RMSEA = 0.047
#>   optimality (ML score): 8.16e-13
#>   starts: 3 of 3 reached the best saturated optimum
as.data.frame(fit)
